extraction.name: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training
extraction.description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing about two trillion tokens. The data is either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses, covering a wide variety of languages (from main European to low-resource) and including a large portion of code data. It is composed of six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: PleIAs
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual (English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian, and others)
extraction.citeAs: Langlais, P.C., Rosas Hinostroza, C., Nee, M., Amett, C., Chizhov, P., Jones, E.K., Girard, I., Mach, D., Stasenko, A., & Yamshchikov, I.P. (2025). Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv:2506.01732.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from various open sources including government portals, cultural heritage institutions (libraries, archives), scientific repositories, code repositories, and web sources. Collection methods included API access, direct dumps, and web crawling where permissible. The process involved aggregating datasets from sources like OpenAlex, Stack Exchange, YouTube, Wikimedia, and various national libraries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include SEC filings, WTO documents, AMF documents, EU Tenders, GATT Library, Europarl, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, Eurovoc, French Open Data, USPTO, UN Digital Library, OECD, Chronicle America, Europeana, Gallica, Biblioteca, LoC Books, US PD Newspapers, New Zealand PD Newspapers, German PD Newspapers, Spanish PD Books, Dutch PD, BnL Newspapers, OpenAlex, ArXiv, Stack v1/v2, Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data manipulation included text segmentation using Segmentext, OCR error detection using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr, OCR correction using OCRonos, PII removal using Microsoft Presidio, and toxicity filtering using the Celadon classifier. Files were filtered by language, format, and license. Sequences of carriage returns were replaced, and files with high digit content were removed.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing steps included: 1) Text segmentation to handle broken/unstructured texts. 2) OCR error detection and correction for digitized documents. 3) PII removal/replacement using Microsoft Presidio. 4) Toxicity detection and filtering/rewriting using Celadon. 5) Filtering by license and language. 6) Removal of low-quality files (e.g., non-informative file types, high digit content). 7) Replacement of line break sequences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were not performed by humans in the traditional sense for the main corpus. However, metadata such as license, language, and collection/domain was attached to each data object. Toxicity labels were used for training the Celadon classifier, which was trained on 2M annotated samples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext, OCRoscope, OCRerrcr, OCRonos, Microsoft Presidio, Celadon, fastText (for language identification)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is an evolving resource. HuggingFace ensures proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility. The dataset is updated as new open data becomes available, with plans to enlarge corpora in African languages.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses were identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values to comply with GDPR and other regulations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to support open science research and development of fully open and auditable LLMs while adhering to legal and regulatory norms. It addresses the 'open data paradox' by providing a large-scale, legally compliant alternative to web-scraped data, potentially reducing legal risks and supporting diverse language models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset acknowledges biases inherent in historical and public domain texts, such as outdated cultural norms regarding ethnic groups, women, and violence. Toxicity filtering was applied to mitigate harmful language. The language distribution is skewed towards European languages, with lower coverage for low-resource and African languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not cover the entire range of available open data. Coverage for low-resource languages is shallow. It is not suitable for instruction-tuning or specialized task fine-tuning. Curation methods (OCR correction, toxicity filtering) do not achieve 100% accuracy. The size (2 trillion tokens) is suitable for smaller models but may be insufficient for very large models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training Large Language Models, creating multimodal datasets, training classifiers, generating synthetic datasets, and developing benchmarks. It is intended for research and entrepreneurial needs in diverse areas of knowledge, particularly for open and auditable LLM development.
